traits.name: Tunneler
traits.value: The crater wurm can burrow through solid rock at half its Burrowing Speed and leaves a 10-foot diameter tunnel in its wake.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The crater wurm makes a Bite attack, then makes Bite attacks against each creature adjacent to the first target.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +14, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 35 (**4d12 + 9**) Piercing damage, and if it is Large or smaller, the target is subjected to the following effect. *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 22. *Failure:* The target is swallowed by the wurm. The target has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, has Total Cover against effects originating from outside the wurm, and takes 36 (**8d8**) Necrotic damage at the start of each of the wurm's turns. A creature that takes this Necrotic damage must also succeed on a DC 19 Constitution saving throw or gain one Contamination level.

If the wurm takes 30+ damage on a single turn from a creature inside it, it must succeed on a DC 21 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which land in spaces within 10 feet of the wurm with the Prone condition. If the wurm dies, a swallowed creature no longer has the Restrained condition and can escape from the corpse using 20 feet of movement, exiting with the Prone condition.

actions.name: Breach
actions.value: The wurm moves up to its Speed, entering the spaces of Large or smaller creatures. Each creature whose space it enters is subjected once to the following effect. At the end of its movement, the wurm can make one Bite attack against a Prone creature as a Bonus Action. *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 22. *Success* The target is pushed 5 feet away from the wurm into a space of its choice. If the target chooses not to move, it suffers the effects of a failure. *Failure:* 35 (**10d6**) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is pushed 10 feet away from the wurm and has the Prone condition.

fluffInfo.value: *Vampiric Zealot*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: Crimson clergy struggle to accept how monstrous they have become. They can't stand the sight of themselves and see their true visage in their reflection.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.value: The clergy can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Vampire Weakness
traits.value: The clergy has the following weaknesses:

entries: *Self-Loathing*. The clergy has Disadvantage on D20 Tests if it can see its reflection.
*Sunlight Hypersensitivity*. The clergy takes 20 Radiant damage if it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

actions.name: Consume
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. *Hit:* 10 (**2d6 + 3**) Necrotic damage. The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken, and the clergy regains Hit Points equal to that amount.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Nature* or *Survival* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks when they take the Study action to examine Crimson Countess, learning the following based on the result:

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Arcane Resistance
fluffInfo.value: You know of the creature's Immunities.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Dangerous Talons
fluffInfo.value: You recognize the creature's Pluck trait.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Bold and Nimble
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the creatures highest and lowest ability scores.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Countess only leaves her clock tower to join in on hunts with her valkyries, but otherwise she prefers the defendable position at the towers highest floor. From here any adventurer who makes it past her soldiers and into her lair can easily be grabbed and thrown off the open balconies, falling to their death.

She is overconfident and will do anything to protect her advantageous position in the city. She only flees if all her minions are dead and she is below 25 Hit Points. If she flees, she will attempt to gather more soldiers and return to reclaim the clock tower at a later date.

traits.name: Aura of Storms
traits.value: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the Crimson Countess takes 10 (**3d6**) Lightning damage.

traits.name: Pluck
traits.value: The Crimson Countess doesn't need to spend extra movement to drag a Medium or smaller creature Grappled by it.

actions.name: The Crimson Countess always takes their turn on Initiative count 20
actions.value: On their turn, the Crimson Countess can use their movement and interaction as normal. However, they do not take an action or Bonus Action on their turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, the Crimson Countess takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

entries: **Grasping Talons**: *Melee Attack Roll:* +8, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 7 (**1d4 + 5**) Piercing damage, and if the target is Medium or smaller, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15).
**Lightning Javelin**: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +8, reach 5 ft. or range 30/60 ft. *Hit:* 14 (**2d8 + 5**) Lightning damage.

actions.name: Aerial Acrobat
actions.value: The Crimson Countess flies up to her Speed without provoking Opportunity Attack action.

actions.name: Frightful Screech (1/Round)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 15, one creature within 120 feet of the Crimson Countess that can hear them. *Failure:* 14 (**4d6**) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition (save ends). While Frightened, the target must take the Dash action and move away from the Crimson Countess by the safest available route on each of its turns unless there is nowhere to move.

actions.name: Lightning Strike (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 15, each creatures in a 60-foot long, 5-foot wide Line. *Failure:* 36 (**8d8**) Lightning damage, and the target has the Shocked condition until the end of its next turn. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: The Crimson Countess chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting them and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on them. The Crimson Countess can use this action even if they would otherwise be unable to take actions, their actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters their game statistics.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *History* or martial melee weapons gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Religion*) checks when taking the Study action to examine a Crimson Knight, learning the following based on the result.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Elite Spawn
fluffInfo.value: You know the Crimson Knight's damage Resistances.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Unholy Magic
fluffInfo.value: You recognize the Crimson Knight can unleash a variety of powerful smites.

fluffInfo.name: (20+) Weaknesses
fluffInfo.value: You are aware the vampire's regeneration is temporarily halted by Radiant damage, and its Vampire Weaknesses.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Crimson Knights form units with other minions and thralls of their vampire masters. Several Crimson Knights may form an elite guard, or one might be attached to lead a contingent of vampire thralls.

In battle, Crimson Knights seek out the most formidable melee combatants to meet head on, disarming them with Crackling Smite. They make use of Unholy Smite to prevent their target from healing, and terrorize them using Wrathful Smite.

A Crimson Knight will give their undead existence to defend their master and hold fast even as they are cut down. If they encounter a foe capable of dealing Radiant damage, they make them the target of their attacks to ensure they can continue to regenerate.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.value: The vampire regains 10 Hit Points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 Hit Point and isn't in sunlight or running water. If the vampire takes Radiant damage or damage from holy water, this trait doesn't function at the start of the vampire's next turn.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.value: The vampire can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Vampire Weaknesses
traits.value: The vampire has the traits described in the "Vampire Weaknesses" sidebar in the Monsters of Drakkenheim.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The vampire makes three attacks. It can replace one attack with a Bite.

actions.name: Claws
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +7, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 9 (**2d4 + 4**) Slashing damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15).

actions.name: Crimson Axe
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +7, reach 5 ft. or range 30/90 ft. *Hit:* 11 (**1d12 + 4**) Force damage, and the target suffers one of the following effects of the vampire's choice. *Hit or Miss:* After being thrown, the axe returns to the vampire's hand.

actions.name: Crackling Smite
actions.value: *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 16. *Failure:* 10 (**3d6**) Thunder damage, and the target has the Shocked condition until the end of its next turn. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Unholy Smite
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 16. *Failure:* 10 (**3d6**) Necrotic damage, and the target can't regain Hit Points until the end of the vampire's next turn. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Wrathful Smite
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 16. *Failure:* 10 (**3d6**) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition (save ends). *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 15, one creature within 5 feet that is willing or has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition. *Failure:* 14 (**3d6 + 4**) Necrotic damage, and the vampire regains Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage dealt.

bonusActions.name: Charge
bonusActions.value: The vampire moves up to its Speed toward a Hostile creature it can see. If it ends this movement within 5 feet of the creature, it has Advantage on the next attack roll it makes against that creature before the end of its turn.

fluffInfo.value: *Splinter of Crooked Power*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: Crooked effigies are bound to the Old Ways, and they recoil from the tools of forging and tinkering—symbols of a growing civilization.

traits.name: Crooked Thorns
traits.value: At the start of each of its turns, the effigy deals 5 (**1d10**) Psychic damage to any creature it is grappling or any creature grappling it.

traits.name: Old Bindings
traits.value: The effigy takes an extra 10 Force damage if it's hit by an attack roll using Smith's Tools or Tinker's Tools (treat as a Club or Light Hammer).

actions.name: Impale
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 8 (**1d10 + 3**) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13) from one of two branch arms. Until the grapple ends, the target has the Restrained condition.

fluffInfo.value: *Crooked Trickster (Anything stolen or gained by trickery)*

entries: **Skills**: deception +5, history +2, sleight of hand +5, stealth +5

traits.name: Trackless Step
traits.value: The crooked hare leaves no tracks, or it leaves the tracks of a Large or smaller creature of its choice. If it doesn't have the Incapacitated condition, it can share the effects of this trait with another creature within 5 feet (no action required).

actions.name: Twisting Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 5 (**1d4 + 3**) Piercing damage plus 7 (**2d6**) Poison damage, and if the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 11 Charisma saving throw or become cursed for 24 hours. The cursed creature's limbs sporadically twist and move in unnatural ways, giving the creature Disadvantage on attack rolls and on ability checks that rely on Charisma.

fluffInfo.value: *Broken Spirit of Betrayal*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: The crooked man can't abide self-sacrifice and withers in its presence.

traits.name: Aversion to Self-Sacrifice
traits.value: The crooked man takes 20 Necrotic damage if he can see a creature willingly take damage or gain a condition in place of someone else, or to someone else's benefit.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The crooked man has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The crooked man makes two Crooked Claw attacks, and he can replace one attack with a use of Snap Limb. He can also use __Confusion__ if available.

actions.name: Crooked Claw
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +11, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 15 (**2d8 + 6**) Slashing damage plus 21 (**6d6**) Psychic damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 16) from one of two claws. Until the grapple ends, the target has the Restrained condition.

actions.name: Snap Limb
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 19, one creature the crooked man is grappling, and that has limbs that can break. *Failure:* 35 (**10d6**) Force damage, and the bones (or equivalent) in one of the target's limbs (crooked man's choice) breaks, causing an appropriate effect below. A broken limb heals in 40 days, or when the creature regains any Hit Points from magic or Regeneration. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Broken Arm
actions.value: Disadvantage on attack rolls. Can't hold anything or manipulate objects with the limb.

actions.name: Broken Leg
actions.value: Speed halved. If the creature takes the Dash action, it must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or have the Prone condition.

actions.name: Broken Wing
actions.value: Fly Speed reduced to 0.

bonusActions.name: Blinking Teleport
bonusActions.value: The crooked man has the Invisible condition for 1 minute and teleports to an unoccupied space he can see within 60 feet. The condition ends immediately after the crooked man deals any damage.

fluffInfo.value: *Fiendish Murder*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: While they might take the form of crows or possess crow bodies, crowstorms are held at bay by drawn images or crafted effigies of crows.

entries: **Immunities**: poison; charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned

traits.name: False Crows
traits.value: The swarm can't enter a space with a drawn or painted image or crafted effigy of a crow. A creature holding such an icon has Advantage on saving throws the swarm forces it to make.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.value: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny crow. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

traits.name: Wing Bind
traits.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 13, any creature (other than a Fiend) with a Fly Speed that starts its turn in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the swarm. *Failure:* The target's Fly Speed is 0 until the start of its next turn.

actions.name: Peck
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 12 (**2d8 + 3**) Piercing damage, or 7 (**1d8 + 3**) Piercing damage if the swarm is *Bloodied*. If the target is a creature, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of the swarm's next turn.

actions.name: Cacophony (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 13, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the swarm. *Failure:* 10 (**3d6**) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the start of the swarm's next turn. *Success* Half damage only.

traits.name: Aura of Dread
traits.value: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of Vladimir von Drakken takes 10 (**3d6**) Necrotic damage.

traits.name: Reborn Transformation
traits.value: When Vladimir von Drakken consumes the blood of six living creatures of level or challenge rating 10 or higher, he transforms into Reborn Vladimir von Drakken. His Initiative doesn't change. If he is destroyed before he can feed sufficiently, he must begin the process again when he rejuvenates.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.value: Vladimir von Drakken regains 30 Hit Points at the start of his turn if he has at least 1 Hit Point remaining.

traits.name: Rejuvenation
traits.value: If Vladimir von Drakken is destroyed in his crypt-starved form, he crumbles into ash and reforms 1d10 days later with all of his Hit Points. His new body appears within his crypt in the Brachenwald. Casting Hallow on the druidic shrine prevents his new body from returning so long as the spell remains in effect.

traits.name: Vampire Weaknesses
traits.value: The vampire has the traits described in the "Vampire Weaknesses" sidebar in the Monsters of Drakkenheim.

actions.name: Vladimir von Drakken always takes his turn on Initiative count 20
actions.value: On his turn, Vladimir von Drakken can use his movement and interaction as normal. However, he does not take an action or Bonus Action on his turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, Vladimir von Drakken takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

entries: **Bloodmourne**: *Melee Attack Roll:* +10, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 26 (**6d6 + 5**) Force damage, and the target has the Bleeding condition (4d4).
**Claws**: *Melee Attack Roll:* +10, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 19 (**4d6 + 5**) Necrotic damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 18).

actions.name: Bite (1/Round)
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 18, one creature within 5 feet that is willing or has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition. *Failure:* 40 (**10d6 + 5**) Necrotic damage. The target's Hit Point Maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and Vladimir von Drakken regains Hit Points equal to that amount. A Humanoid killed by this effect and then buried in the ground rises the following night as a Vampire Spawn under Vladimir von Drakken's control.

actions.name: Terrifying Glare
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 18, one creature Vladimir von Drakken can see within 120 feet. *Failure:* 21 (**6d6**) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Failure by 5 or More: While Frightened, the target has the Paralyzed condition.

actions.name: Shadow Step (1/Round)
actions.value: Vladimir von Drakken teleports to an unoccupied space he can see within 60 feet that is in Dim Light or Darkness. He has Advantage on the next melee attack he makes before the end of this round.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: Vladimir von Drakken chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting him and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on him. He can use this action even if he would otherwise be unable to take actions, his actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters his game statistics.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Survival* or *Nature* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks to Study a Crystalline Dreg, learning the following based on their result:

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Light Absorption
fluffInfo.value: You recognize the creaturea has Resistance to Radiant damage.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Reflecting Attacks
fluffInfo.value: You learn of the Dreg's Refracted Beam attack.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Prone to Shattering
fluffInfo.value: You understand the creature's Vulnerability to Bludgeoning damage.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Crystalline Dreg is quite literally a glass cannon. It prefers to stay behind other Dregs, blasting its foes with its beam attacks and absorbing any elemental damage to alter its attacks. If an enemy who can deal Bludgeoning damage is present, the Crystalline Dreg will flee from that creature and attempt to kill them from a distance, knowing it is their biggest threat. The Dreg tends to focus on enemies approaching with melee weapons over anyone using elemental damage. If the front line of Dregs that the Crystalline Dreg often uses as shield is gone, or if the Crystalline Dregs are outnumbered and threatened with melee combat, they attempt to flee.

fluffInfo.value: It uses its Eye Laser to disintegrate enemies into a fine delerium dust. The Cyclopean Hulk focuses its power on blasting enemies from afar or slamming them into the ground if they get close. It will then Wink out of existence, reappearing every few seconds to deliver a devastating blast from its eye before vanishing again. Cyclopean Hulks usually fight to the end, and rarely flee.

actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +8, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 18 (**3d8 + 5**) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Eye Laser
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 14, each creature in a 60-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. *Failure:* 18 (**4d8**) Force damage. *Success* Half damage. *Failure or Success*: If the target is a creature and this damage reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it disintegrates into a pile of fine delerium dust.

bonusActions.name: Wink (Recharge 4-6)
bonusActions.value: The hulk vanishes from the Material Plane and is transported to the Space Between Worlds. At the start of its next turn, it returns to an unoccupied space of its choice within 10 feet of the space it vanished from. If no unoccupied space is available within that range, it appears in the nearest unoccupied space (chosen at random if more than one space is equally near).

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.value: Dagon can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day)
traits.value: If Dagon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: One With the Sea
traits.value: When Dagon drops to 0 Hit Points or would be killed outright, it instead transforms into a swirling body of water. At the start of each of Dagon's turns, it gains one recovery point but otherwise cannot use actions or legendary actions other than Relentless Horror. When it gains its fourth recovery point, its maximum Hit Points return to normal if they have been reduced and it regains all lost Hit Points. It reforms its physical body in a space of its choice within 10 miles of its location. It then loses all recovery points.

If Dagon is the target of a __Banishment__ spell cast with a 9th-level spell slot while in this cloud form, it automatically fails its saving throw and is instead sent to the deepest corner of the ocean where it slumbers for 6d10 years.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.value: Dagon deals double damage to objects and structures.

traits.name: Spectral Waves
traits.value: Storm-tossed waves formed of magical force swirl around Dagon in a 120-foot Emanation originating from him. Creatures without a Swim Speed treat this area as Difficult Terrain and take 10 Force damage if they end their turn in this area. Flying creatures that end their turn in this area must make DC 24 Strength saving throws, gaining the Prone condition on a failed save.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: Dagon makes four Slashing Claw attacks.

actions.name: Slashing Claw
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +17, Reach 20 ft. *Hit:* 21 (**2d10 + 10**) Slashing damage and the target is pushed up to 10 feet away from Dagon and gains the Prone condition.

actions.name: Hungry Tide (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 24, creatures of Dagon's choice within 120 ft. of it; *First Failure:* The target takes 11 (**2d10**) Force damage, and gains the Restrained condition until the end of its next turn, when it repeats the save. *Second Failure:* The target takes 4d20 (22) Force damage its Speed is reduced to 0 and cannot be increased until it uses an action to make a successful DC 24 Strength (*Athletics*) check.

traits.name: Training
traits.value: The commoner has proficiency in one skill of the DM's choice and has Advantage whenever it makes an ability check using that skill.

actions.name: Club
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +2, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 2 (**1d4**) Bludgeoning damage.

fluffInfo.value: In the first round of combat, the Dark Confessor casts __Spirit Guardians__. It uses its Claws to attack anyone who comes within its melee reach. The Dark Confessor then proceeds to attack with its Spiritual Maul.
If there are enemies grouped close to one another, the Dark
Confessor uses Unholy Light on them.
The Dark Confessor flees if it is below 50 Hit Points or takes steady Radiant damage.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: A Dark Growth is a simple-minded plant. It uses Mimicry to lure passing creatures towards it, often mimicking the sounds of children or people in need. It entangles and infests any target near it, infecting it with its spores. The creature is a stationary plant and does not flee.

traits.value: The dark growth can mimic any sounds it has heard, including voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (*Insight*) check.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.value: The dark growth regains 10 Hit Points at the start of its turn. If the Dark Growth takes Fire or Radiant damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the dark growth's next turn. The dark growth dies only if it starts its turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The dark growth makes three attacks: two with its Entangling Vines and one with its Infection Spores.

actions.name: Entangling Vines
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +7, reach 30 ft. *Hit:* 8 (**1d8 + 4**) Piercing damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15) and the target has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

actions.name: Infection Spores
actions.value: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +7, range 60 ft. *Hit:* 18 (**4d6 + 4**) Necrotic damage, and if the target is a creature, it is subjected to the following effect. *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 14. *Failure:* The target is infected with a disease called Dark Decay. Instead of acting normally on its turn, the target must move toward the closest creature that isn't infected with Dark Decay and make one melee attack against it. If the attack hits, the target of that attack must also make a saving throw against Dark Decay. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save. Subsequent Failures: The target gains one Contamination level. Third Success: The disease ends.

An infected creature that dies or undergoes a Monstrous Transformation becomes a Dark Growth Shambler. A __Lesser Restoration__ spell or similar magic that removes diseases ends Dark Decay, as does any magic that removes Contamination levels.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The dark growth shambler makes two Claw attacks and one Infectious Bite attack.

actions.name: Claw
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +6, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 10 (**2d6 + 3**) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Infectious Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +6, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 10 (**2d6 + 3**) Necrotic damage, and if the target is a creature, it is subjected to the following effect. *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 14. *Failure:* The target is infected with a disease called Dark Decay. Instead of acting normally on its turn, the target must move toward the closest creature that isn't infected with Dark Decay and make one melee attack against it. If the attack hits, the target of that attack must also make a saving throw against Dark Decay. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save. Subsequent Failures: The target gains one Contamination level. Third Success: The disease ends.

An infected creature that dies or undergoes a Monstrous Transformation becomes a Dark Growth Shambler. A __Lesser Restoration__ spell or similar magic that removes diseases ends Dark Decay, as does any magic that removes Contamination levels.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Strong and Tough

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Deep Dreg Warriors attack from the water, throwing their spears and diving back under the surface as added protection against ranged retaliation. When they engage in melee, the warriors use their Net to restrain their foes, and make melee attacks (with the bonus damage from Catch of the Day) to knock them Unconscious.

Deep Dregs Warriors flee whenever they are outnumbered or if they are reduced below half their maximum Hit Points. They swim to safety rather than die fighting, and prefer to fall back and retaliate after gathering reinforcements.

The Deep Knight will defend the other Deep Dregs to the death. If it is the last one standing it will attempt to flee, but as long as there are allies to protect, it will stay and fight.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Deep Sirens are the generals and confidants to the Duchess and often serve as the eyes and ears of their mistress. They use their Illusory Appearance to walk among humanoids and observe them, planning and plotting the attacks of the Deep Dregs. Once it has gathered information, a Deep Siren returns to the Duchess, and is often sent with the Deep Dregs to storm beaches, infiltrate sewers, or take over cities on stormy nights.
The siren doesn't like being in close combat, and always attempts to use __Misty Step__ to move to a more beneficial position, then unleash Storm Lash or spellcasting upon their foes.
They flee if surrounded, if outnumbered, or if they feel the battle is not going in their favor.

actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +7, reach 5 ft. or range 90 ft. *Hit:* 18 (**4d8**) Thunder damage, and the target is pushed up to 10 feet away from the deep siren.

actions.name: Discordant Song (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
actions.value: *Intelligence Saving Throw:* DC 15, each creature of the deep siren's choice in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the deep siren. *Failure:* 21 (**6d6**) Psychic damage, and the target must roll 1d6 and subtract the result from each D20 Test it makes. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute.

actions.name: Illusory Appearance
actions.value: The deep siren covers herself and anything she is wearing or carrying with a magical illusion that makes her look like another creature of her general size and shape. The illusion ends if the siren takes a Bonus Action to end it or if she dies.

The changes wrought by this effect fail to hold up to physical inspection. For example, the siren could appear to have smooth skin, but someone touching them would feel their fishy flesh. Otherwise, a creature must take an action to visually inspect the illusion and succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence (*Investigation*) check to discern that the siren is disguised.

bonusActions.name: Misty Step

fluffInfo.value: *Poisoned Subterranean Wretch*

fluffInfo.name: Secret

traits.name: Explosive Death

traits.name: Fragrance Aversion

traits.name: Tunneler

traits.name: Delerium Healing

traits.name: Alien Intellect
traits.value: The dragon is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (*Insight*) checks made to ascertain the dragon's intentions or sincerity have Disadvantage.

actions.name: Multiattack

A wounded Delerium Dreg typically responds with fury and rage, attacking whatever damaged it last without regard to its personal wellbeing. fluffInfo.value: An __Alienist__ looking to permanently control the mind of their victim may opt to remove the brain altogether, killing the patient and resurrecting the mind as its own sentient entity. Somewhere within this process the brain loses its sense of self and any connection it had to the former body it held, becoming an organism made up entirely of electrical synapses and controlled thoughts. The Disembodied Psyche is then subject to several arduous experiments to heighten its fortitude and mental capabilities, giving the creature forms of telepathy and telekinesis.

The now-undead form of this controlled consciousness can be unleashed upon the foes of the alienist and even take over the bodies of other victims, putting them in a controlled and obedient state for the alienist to perform even more mental experiments on, or use as a puppet against their enemies.

The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 Hit Points or the psyche leaves as a Bonus Action. Whenever the target takes damage, it repeats the save, ending the possession on a success. fluffInfo.value: *The mastermind behind some of the worst things to ever find in a basement. Watch out because even your fallen allies can be enemies.*

Perhaps no apothecary is a more prolific creator of monsters than the Reanimator, and amongst them, Dr. Everett Freed is perhaps the most infamous. A gifted professor of anatomy and medicine at Altbruke University, Dr. Everett Freed served as a field medic and surgeon during the Westemär Civil War, where the brutality and chaos of war allowed him to clandestinely begin his experiments with the fallen or grievously wounded soldiers thrust into his care. The sights of the war caused him to see the frailty of the human form—the cries of pain and agony of the wounded collected in the fields disgusted him with their feeble, broken bodies. Deep within himself welled the desire to create a perfect soldier, a warrior who would not bend or break in battle.

During the war, one of Dr. Freed's duties included triaging casualties to determine who could be saved or recover. Unbeknownst to his commanders, Dr. Freed used his position to manipulate the diagnosis, choosing ideal specimens for his experiments, individuals who would then be listed amongst the slain and missing.

fluffInfo.name: Reanimator Minions
fluffInfo.value: It's possible Dr. Freed was the first to create many creatures. He is most well known as the first to create Reautomata. In the process of making his magnum opus, Freed built creatures such as the __Body Snatcher__, __Cerebrograft__, the __Ripper__, and the __Stitcher__. Freed's experiments did not stop there, and in many ways his practice ascended the body alone thanks to his collaborations with the Alienist Dr. Sina Rienks, eventually transforming himself into a __Think Tank__.

fluffInfo.name: Mind Over Body
fluffInfo.value: One of Freed's infamous gambits was to remove his brain from his own body, placing it into a body double. Eventually, Freed became a Think Tank, able to remotely control brainless bodies from his hidden sanctum.

entries: **Personality Trait:** I am always calm and composed, especially when explaining the 'necessary' cruelty of my experiments
**Ideal:** Progress demands sacrifice; the advancement of knowledge justifies all actions, no matter how gruesome.
**Bond:** I still possess the first successful reanimation I ever created: the preserved head of a beloved family member. It's both my proudest achievement and my darkest secret.

**Flaw:** I am obsessed with the perfection and infallibility of my creations, often dismissing any evidence of their defects, uncontrollable behavior, and horrific appearances. I never accept any failure as my fault.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Prior to combat, Freed casts __False Life__ and __Death Ward__ on himself, and perhaps any allies joining him in battle. He does not engage in combat without creations by his side. If Freed is caught alone, he doesn't fight; he flees. However, when supported by his loyal creations, he can be overconfident and brash, secure that his bodyguards will keep him safe from harm. Freed always remains within 10 feet of one or more creations so he can use his Bodyguard Reaction reliably.

On his turn, Freed uses Electric Jolt and Necrotic Blast to hammer his foes, while directing a favored creation with Creator's Command. Should one of his minions be brought down, he uses Reanimate and immediately sends it back into the action with Creator's Command.

Freed uses Touch of Death against a particularly loathsome foe, one who harries him with dangerous abilities, or who he especially wishes to slay. All the while, he threatens his enemies by telling them his plans for their body parts once he's killed them.

A Frightened target takes the Dash action and moves away from the drakkenhob by the safest route on each of its turns unless there's nowhere to move. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. *Success* Half damage only.

bonusActions.value: The drakkenhob lets out a wolf-like howl and magically summons three hunting hounds (use the Wolf stat block) that appear in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of it. The hounds take their turn immediately after the drakkenhob on the same Initiative count, and they obey the drakkenhob's mental commands. The hounds vanish when they or the drakkenhob drop to 0 Hit Points, or when the drakkenhob uses this Bonus Action again.

fluffInfo.value: *Devourer of Nightmares*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: Dream eaters are confused by the intricate patterns on moth wings, and it disrupts their own colorful hypnosis.

traits.name: Flyby
traits.value: The dream eater doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

traits.name: Moth Ward
traits.value: A creature holding a moth's wing automatically succeeds on saving throws against the dream eater's Hypnotic Wings.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.value: The dream eater can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The dream eater makes two Talons attacks and can use Devour Dreams.

actions.name: Talons
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +8, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 11 (**2d6 + 4**) Slashing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of two talons, and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

actions.name: Devour Dreams
actions.value: The dream eater unfurls its tongue and devours the dreams from a creature's mind. *Charisma Saving Throw:* DC 16, a creature the dream eater is grappling, or a creature within 5 feet of it that has the Incapacitated condition (Incapacitated creatures fail automatically). *Failure:* 18 (**4d8**) Psychic damage, and the creature's Charisma score decreases by 1d6. A creature reduced to 0 Charisma by this effect doesn't recover lost Charisma when it finishes a Long Rest, and it has the Incapacitated condition until its mind is restored with a __Greater Restoration__, __Heal__, or __Wish__ spell. *Success* Half damage only.

bonusActions.name: Hypnotic Wings
bonusActions.value: The dream eater's wings shine with dazzling rainbow colors until the start of its next turn, emitting Bright Light in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the dream eater and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet. *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 16, each creature in the dream eater's Bright Light. *Failure:* Until the start of the dream eater's next turn, the target has the Incapacitated condition, and its Speed is 0.

entries: **Languages**: all languages known before the curse

traits.name: Aura of Confusion
traits.value: A creature that starts its turn or moves within 25 feet of a Dream Whisperer must succeed on a DC 13 Intelligence saving throw or be affected as if they had failed a save against the __Confusion__ spell.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The Dream Whisperer has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.value: The Dream Whisperer can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The Dream Whisperer makes three Claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.value: *Melee Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 13 (**2d8 + 4**) Slashing damage, and the target is subjected to the following effect. *Intelligence Saving Throw:* DC 13. *Failure:* The Dream Whisperer gains Advantage on attack rolls against the target for 1 minute, and the target rolls on the Lost Memories table.

table.title: Lost Memories
rows: The target becomes deeply suspicious of a character or NPC of the GM's choice. They gain the following flaw: "I know they are seeking to betray me. I have to act first—it's me or them!"
The target forgets all memories of a loved one of the GM's choice. The next time the target sees them, it's as if they are meeting them for the first time.
The target becomes stricken with doubt and gains the following flaw: ""The world is out to get me, and I can't win. I may as well give up now."
The target forgets how to speak in one language known, decided by the GM.
The target forgets the location of something important to them, of the GM's choice. It may be the location of a goal, their home settlement, or a hidden treasure.
The target loses an inconsequential memory such as what they ate a few nights ago or the name of an unimportant NPC.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Religion* or *Survival* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks when taking the Study action to examine a Druid of the Sanguine Rite, learning the following based on the result.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Unrelenting Unlife

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Bloody Renewal
fluffInfo.value: You learn of the creature's Bloodthorn Whip attack and Plasma Absorption trait

fluffInfo.value: You know their highest and lowest ability scores

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The druid of the blood rites uses dark magic to twist the lifeforce of other creatures. The druid uses its bloodthorn whip to inflict a series of open wounds upon its foes, and then feeds on their lifeforce by pulling it through their wounds using plasma absorption.
When not directly engaged in combat, the druids attempt to charm a group of foes and convince them to partake in their blood rituals, using their life force as sacrifice to empower one of their own.
If the druids are directly confronted with greater numbers, or their health is below half, they attempt to flee.

traits.name: Blood Sacrifice
traits.value: A creature with the Restrained condition also has the Helpless condition against the vampire's attacks.

traits.name: Plasma Absorption
traits.value: Each time a creature takes damage from the Bleeding condition while within 30 feet of the vampire, the vampire regains Hit Points equal to the damage dealt.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.value: The vampire regains 10 Hit Points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 Hit Point and isn't in sunlight or running water. If the vampire takes Radiant damage or damage from holy water, this trait doesn't function at the start of the vampire's next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The vampire makes three attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Draining Bite or Spellcasting.

actions.name: Claws
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +7, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 9 (**2d4 + 4**) Slashing damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15).

actions.name: Bloodthorn Whip
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +9, reach 30 ft. *Hit:* 17 (**3d8 + 5**) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Bleeding condition (4d4).

actions.name: Draining Bite
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 17, one creature within 5 feet that is willing or has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition. *Failure:* 14 (**3d6 + 4**) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Weakened condition (save ends).

actions.name: Bloodroots (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 17, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the vampire. *Failure:* 21 (**6d6**) Piercing damage, and the target has the Restrained condition (save ends). *Success* Half damage only.

fluffInfo.value: Du'ulora are spirits of fury that feed on anger and inspire rage in mortals. A du'ulora is a maelstrom of eyes and wings, bound together by flesh that seems like solidified shadow. It can extend up to three tentacles from this dark mass. A du'ulora can turn a victim's anger into manifested heat; in battle, it grapples its victims and burns them with their own fury.

fluffInfo.name: Manipulating Fury
fluffInfo.value: While they feed on anger and hatred, du'ulora rarely act rashly. They are cunning and calculating strategists who excel at inspiring fury in others and turning it against them. In battle this can cause their victims to lower their guard and even to strike their own allies in heedless rage. As servants of the Dreaming Dark, the du'ulora craft dreams that stir buried anger and incite hatred; they excel at igniting feuds and inspiring vendettas. So where a tsucora agent of the Dreaming Dark manipulates peoples' fears and a hashalaq employs seduction, the du'ulora excel at inciting violence.

fluffInfo.name: The Fists of Dal Quor
fluffInfo.value: The du'ulora are martial champions of the quori. They thrive on conflict and love to personally crush their enemies. While they enjoy fighting in the vanguard, the du'ulora are also skilled strategists. In Dal Quor , the du'ulora command squads of tsucora and lesser quori. In Riedra, military commanders are typically Inspired bound to du'ulora spirits.

fluffInfo.name: Rage Against The Darkness
fluffInfo.value: The du'ulora bound to the kalashtar serve the light, but they still manipulate fury. Du'ulora kalashtar learn to harness and channel their own aggression, and are often Fighters or Barbarians; others are dispassionate Monks, who provoke rage in their enemies while never allowing it to distract them from their goals.

traits.name: All-Around Vision
traits.value: The quori can't be *surprised* while it isn't Incapacitated.

traits.name: Aura of Fury
traits.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 16, any creature that starts its turn in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the quori. *Failure:* The target becomes enraged. While enraged, the target has Advantage on all melee attack rolls, and all attack rolls made against the target have Advantage.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The quori has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Track Hatred
traits.value: When the quori deals damage to any creature, it forms a psychic link with the target for 24 hours. During that time, the quori has advantage on Wisdom (*Survival*) checks to track the target. The quori can attempt to track the target at any range, even if it is on another plane of existence. Abilities such as the __Pass Without Trace__ spell or the Ranger's Nature's Veil feature do not impede the quori's ability to track its target. The quori remains alert to danger even when it is tracking while traveling.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The quori makes three Tentacle attacks.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +9, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 12 (**2d6 + 5**) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (**2d6**) Fire damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 17) from one of three tentacles. While Grappled, the target takes 10 (**3d6**) Fire damage and 10 (**3d6**) Psychic damage at the start of each of the quori's turns.

actions.name: Possession (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Charisma Saving Throw:* DC 16, one Humanoid the quori can see within 5 feet. *Failure:* The target is possessed by the quori; the quori disappears and the target has the Incapacitated condition and loses control of its body. The quori now controls the body, but the target retains awareness. The quori can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that specifically target Aberrations. The quori's game statistics are the same, except it uses the possessed target's Speed, as well as the target's Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution modifiers.

The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 Hit Points or the quori leaves as a Bonus Action. When the possession ends, the quori appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target, and the target is immune to this quori's Possession for 24 hours. *Success* The target is immune to this quori's Possession for 24 hours.

actions.name: Recall Agony (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 16, one creature the quori can see within 60 feet. *Failure:* 67 (**15d8**) Psychic damage. *Success* Half damage.

traits.name: Customized Poison
traits.value: The assassin prepares and applies specialized poisons to its weapons. The first time each turn that the assassin deals weapon damage to a creature, choose one of the following:

entries: **Abduction**: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 15. *Failure:* The target has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. The condition ends if the target takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it. *Success* The target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn.
**Debilitation**: The target takes 17 (**5d6**) Poison damage, and has the Poisoned condition until the start of the assassin's next turn.
**Suffocation**: The target has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. While Poisoned in this way, the target can't speak or breathe.

traits.name: Evasion
traits.value: If the assassin is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, the assassin instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and only half damage if it fails. It can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Heavy Crossbow

fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Nature* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks to Study an Effulgent Cnidarian, learning the following based on their result:

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Aberrant Resistance
fluffInfo.value: You recognize the monster's Immunities and Resistances.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Hypnotic Color Change

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Weak but Aware
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the monster's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Effulgent Cnidarians are not predatorial—they only want to bask in the glow of delerium crystals, feeding slowly on the arcane energies they emit. They are, however, protective of their food sources. If creatures venture into an area of heavy delerium crystallization, they are sure to find a few Cnidarians bobbing about. The Cnidarian prefers to use its Hallucinogenic Bioluminescence to dissuade threats from engaging, instead hoping to cause its enemies to kill one another. The Cnidarians feed on creatures under its hypnosis, absorbing their essence through its tendrils. If attacked, it uses its Reflexive Flash and attempts to move away from its threats, often floating straight up as quickly as it can and out of the reach of danger.
Cnidarians do not stay around to fight. If all targets have avoided its charm and are actively attacking it, it abandons its food source to seek other safer areas.

traits.name: Altered Reality
traits.value: The cnidarian has the Invisible condition for creatures Charmed by it.

traits.name: Hallucinogenic Bioluminescence
traits.value: A creature that starts its turn within 60 feet of the cnidarian and can see it is subjected to the following effect unless the cnidarian chooses otherwise. *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 16. *Failure:* The target has the Charmed condition (save ends). While Charmed, the target regards all other creatures as enemies except the cnidarian, whom it regards as an ally.

Whenever the target makes an attack or casts a detrimental spell, it must choose its target at random from the creatures it can see within range. If a creature provokes an Opportunity Attack action from the target, it must make the attack, if able. If the target ends its turn without taking an Attack or Magic action, it takes 14 (**4d6**) Psychic damage.

Unless *surprised*, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls against the cnidarian until the start of its next turn. If the creature looks at the cnidarian in the meantime, that creature must immediately make the saving throw.

traits.name: Neon Illumination

actions.name: Tendrils

If it succeeds, its attacks against the target are critical hits on die rolls of 18 or higher for the next minute or until it uses Surgical Eye against a different target. If the elder thing succeeds on this check a second time against the same creature, its attacks against the target are instead critical hits on die rolls of 16 or higher for the next minute or until it uses Surgical Eye against a different target.

traits.value: Eldrick can cast a spell from Spellcasting without expending a use of it.

traits.name: Magic Resistance

traits.name: Warding Aura
traits.value: Eldrick projects a 30-foot Emanation of warding magic. The first time on each turn that a creature within the Emanation deals damage or casts a spell on Eldrick, that creature takes 14 (**4d6**) Force damage and is pushed 10 feet away from Eldrick.

actions.name: Eldrick always takes his turn on Initiative count 20
actions.value: On his turn, Eldrick can use his movement and interaction as normal. However, he does not take an action or Bonus Action on his turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, Eldrick takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

actions.name: Prismatic Blast
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +15, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. *Hit:* 27 (**4d10 + 6**) Cold, Fire, or Lightning damage (Eldrick's choice).

actions.name: Teleport
actions.value: Eldrick teleports to an unoccupied space he can see within 60 feet.

actions.name: Chain Lightning (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: Eldrick casts __Chain Lightning__, using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

actions.name: Dispel Magic (1/Round)
actions.value: Eldrick casts __Dispel Magic__, using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: Eldrick chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting him and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on him. Eldrick can use this action even if he would otherwise be unable to take actions, his actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters his game statistics.

fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Nature* or *Survival* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks when they Study an Eldritch Cataclysm, learning the following based on their result:

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Amalgamation of Energies
fluffInfo.value: You learn the creature's Immunities, as well as its Air Form trait.

fluffInfo.name: (20+) An Octarine Storm
fluffInfo.value: You recognize its Chain Lightning, Meteor Strike, Quake, and Icy Bolt actions.

fluffInfo.name: (25+) Exceedingly Resilient
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Eldritch Cataclysms rule the skies, and never willingly descend to the ground. Instead, it rains down lightning, meteors, and icy blasts from above. The temperamental nature of these elementals means they delight in attacking with a variety of elements, and seldom use the same action two rounds in a row. They enjoy using their Meteor Strike on targets they've Frozen with Icy Bolt, and delight in using their Cyclonic Storm to blow away weapons and equipment dropped by targets of their Chain Lightning.

These enraged creatures revel in destruction but have little conception that anything could actually pose a threat to them. When confronted with a foe able to withstand their onslaught, they treat it as a personal affront, and furiously focus their subsequent attacks upon them occasionally to the exclusion of all else. Despite this single-minded strategy, an Eldritch Cataclysm can recognize when a creature is resistant or immune to its elemental attacks and tries to use only the most effective powers against its chosen target.

traits.name: Air Form
traits.value: The eldritch cataclysm can enter a Hostile creature's space and stop there. It can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.

traits.name: Cyclonic Storm
traits.value: The eldritch cataclysm emits a 120-foot Emanation of high winds that disperse gases and vapors and extinguish unprotected flames. Ranged attacks that pass through the area have Disadvantage. Objects that are not worn or carried are blown away 1d6 x 5 feet in a random direction. A creature that starts its turn in the Emanation is subjected to the following effect. *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 17 (flying creatures have Disadvantage). *Failure:* The target has the Slowed condition until the start of its next turn. Failure by 5 or More: The target is flung 1d6 x 5 feet in a random direction, landing with the Prone condition.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The eldritch cataclysm uses Chain Lighting or Icy Bolt, then uses Meteor Stike or Quake.

actions.name: Chain Lightning
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +12, range 120 ft. *Hit:* 21 (**3d8 + 7**) Lightning damage, the target has the Shocked condition until the end of the cataclysm's next turn, and the lightning leaps to another creature of the cataclysm's choice within 15 feet of the first target. The cataclysm makes a separate __Chain Lightning__ attack against the target. The cataclysm can make any number of __Chain Lightning__ attacks in this way, but a creature can be targeted only once each time the cataclysm takes this action.

actions.name: Icy Bolt
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +12, range 120 ft. *Hit:* 21 (**3d8 + 7**) Cold damage. *Hit or Miss:* The target and each creature within 5 feet of it are subjected to the following effect. *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 17. *Failure:* 18 (**4d8**) Cold damage, and the target has the Frozen condition (DC 17).

actions.name: Meteor Strike
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 17, each creature in a 15-foot radius, 40-foot tall Cylinder centered on a point the cataclysm can see within 120 feet. *Failure:* 18 (**4d8**) Fire damage plus 18 (**4d8**) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Quake
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 17, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the cataclysm. *Failure:* 28 (**8d6**) Thunder damage, and the target has the Prone condition. *Success* Half damage only.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Escape Reality

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Dull and Diffident

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Eldritch Crawlers weave together fractured timelines, and slip in and out of the Space Between Worlds with ease. They create their own Thin Places and travel through them back and forth as needed. When under attack, Eldritch Crawlers bend and alter the realities they exist in to shift to one where they are more likely to survive. They teleport around the battlefield and vanish into the Space Between Worlds as they need to, using Void Walker and their Fractured Reality Reaction, only to reemerge and attack their prey with Contaminated Venom.

traits.name: Fully Contaminated
traits.value: The eldritch crawler is immune to Contamination and has Advantage on saving throws against contaminated spells. The eldritch crawler may cast contaminated spells even though it does not gain Contamination levels.

traits.name: Delerium Healing
traits.value: As an action, the eldritch crawler can touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) Hit Points. Once the eldritch crawler has used a delerium shard in this way, the shard can't be used in this manner again for 24 hours.

traits.name: Alien Intellect
traits.value: The eldritch crawler is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (*Insight*) checks made to ascertain the eldritch crawler's intentions or sincerity have Disadvantage.

traits.name: Insectoid Limbs
traits.value: The eldritch crawler can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. It ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

actions.name: Bite

actions.name: Contaminated Venom
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 12, one target within 40 feet. *Failure:* 18 (**4d8**) Necrotic damage, and the target gains one Contamination level. *Success* Half damage only.

bonusActions.name: Void Walker
bonusActions.value: The eldritch crawler climbs through a tear in reality, traveling from the Material Plane to the Space Between Worlds or vice versa.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Psychic Powers

It teleports from place to place using its Flickerjump, setting alight creatures and objects using its Dancing Flames. If possible, it tries to remain close to Burning targets to keep them on fire within its Enduring Flame aura.

Within the smoking ruins of Drakkenheim, Entropic Flames love to set buildings, furniture, and other objects on fire. They quickly turn the battlefield into a roiling inferno, one which cannot be extinguished easily thanks to their presence.

The Entropic Watcher focuses its gaze upon its prey and unleashes its eye beams towards it, knowing that if it can hold its gaze, the creature will succumb to the watcher's blasts much easier. It will use its Force Barrier and Shadow Crash to force its victims into an optimal position for it to strike, and grab them with its tendrils, holding them readily in its Withering Gaze.
If the Entropic Watcher is reduced to less than 50 Hit Points, it attempts to flee.

Creatures in the Line have Vulnerability to Necrotic damage and can't regain Hit Points.

entries: **Tendrils**: *Melee Attack Roll:* +10, reach 40 ft. *Hit:* 17 (**3d8 + 4**) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 (**2d8**) Necrotic damage, and if the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 18). While Grappled, the target has the Restrained condition. The entropic watcher has ten tendrils, each of which can grapple one creature.

**Insanity Beam (1/Round)**: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +10, range 60 ft. *Hit:* 22 (**4d10**) Necrotic damage, and the beam leaps to another target. The entropic watcher makes another Insanity Beam attack against a new target within 30 feet of the first. A creature can be targeted by only one Insanity Beam per turn. For each additional creature the beam hits, its damage increases by 5 (1d10).

actions.name: Shadow Crash (Recharge 5-6)

A creature that ends its turn in the area takes 36 (**8d8**) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Contaminated Grasp
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 18, one creature Grappled by the entropic watcher. *Failure:* 16 (**3d10**) Necrotic damage, and the target gains one Contamination level. *Success* Half damage.

The wall lasts for 1 minute or until the entropic watcher has the Incapacitated condition or dies. The wall appears in any orientation it chooses, and can be free floating or resting on a solid surface. If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (the entropic watcher's choice).

Nothing can physically pass through the wall. It is immune to all damage and can't be dispelled by __Dispel Magic__. A __Disintegrate__ spell destroys the wall instantly, however. The wall also extends into the Ethereal Plane, blocking ethereal travel through the wall.

actions.name: Epic Resistance

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Executioner is not a foe to be defeated, but rather an obstacle to be avoided or a danger to escape. It is a reminder of the callous and uncontrollable dangers present in Drakkenheim. The Executioner's combat tactics vary based on whether it detects low-level characters trespassing in Slaughterstone Square or high-level characters trying to defeat the machine itself. The Executioner pursues its targets within Slaughterstone Square, but never leaves the plaza.

When the Executioner detects creatures trespassing on Slaughterstone Square, it responds first by using Summon Grasping Shadows, followed up by Death Grip to try to prevent their escape. Meanwhile, it uses Lumber Forward to gain ground. You should embrace clever solutions that characters invent to escape or bypass the Executioner. As long as your players aren't trying to destroy it, the Executioner will only use Guillotine Blade against a Restrained target within its melee range, and does not make ranged attacks nor activate its Necrotic Vents aura.

However, should your players engage the Executioner directly in combat, do not pull any punches. They have made an incredibly foolish mistake by confronting a well-telegraphed deathtrap and should be served their just desserts. It activates its Necrotic Vents, and then relentlessly attacks with its Guillotine Blade. The Executioner throws the massive weapon to hit targets trying to avoid it in melee, or those that try to harm it with ranged weapons or spells. If it encounters any impediment in its way (such as a __Wall of Force__), it crushes it with Destroyer.

fluffInfo.value: *I admire their divine focus but it's the controlling you with ghosts thing where they lose me.*

An Exorcist comes prepared to deal with evil entities, sinister spirits, and fearsome fiends. Equipped with their holy symbol, a book of prayers, and a bag of ritualistic baubles, Exorcists stand ready to face the most unnatural and otherworldly entities of the realms. Some Exorcists, however, are so familiar with the ways of the undead, they can summon spirits into hosts. In some rare cases, Exorcists allow demons to inhabit the living.

fluffInfo.name: Exorcists Minions
fluffInfo.value: Exorcists deal with all manner of entities. They can call forth Specters, Ghosts, Demons, Wraiths, and other extraplanar entities. The most horrifying creation of the Exorcist is the Soulbound Host, which occurs when an Exorcist allows themself to be a vessel for demonic, extraplanar, or fairy entities, attempting to harness the power of such beings. Most are driven mad during the process.

entries: **Personality Trait:** I speak to the dead often, sometimes when I am not even sure if they are there..
**Bond:** The understanding of life and death grants us power over the planes that few have dared to grasp.
**Ideal:** It is in control of demons and ghosts that we will transcend to our true potential.
**Flaw:** I am sure I have the strength within me to host a demon or spirit without succumbing to its will.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Exorcist relies on its divine weapons and direct combat skills. They often reside in locations that have natural hazards where they can use their Grasping Ghosts to force enemies into danger. Hazards could include burning braziers, spiked pits, or a pool of blessed acid. If any foe has a summoned creature, the Exorcist dispatches it using Expel Evil, and destroy any undead foes with Last Rites.
If the Exorcist is in a losing situation, they attempt to use Spiritual Healing on themself before fleeing.

traits.name: Blessed Weapons
traits.value: When the Exorcist hits with any weapon, the weapon unleashes holy fire, causing the target to have the Burning condition (4d6 Radiant; included in the attacks below).

actions.name: Multiattack

actions.name: Blessed Crossbow
actions.value: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +7, range 80/320 ft. *Hit:* 9 (**1d10 + 4**) Piercing damage, and the target has the Burning condition (4d6 Radiant).

actions.name: Grasping Ghost
actions.value: *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 15, one creature the exorcist can see within 60 feet. *Failure:* 18 (**4d8**) Necrotic damage, and the target is moved 30 feet in a horizontal direction of the exorcist's choice. At the end of this movement, the target has the Immobilized condition until the end of the exorcist's next turn. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Expel Evil (1/Day)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 15, each Celestial, Fey, Fiend, and Undead that can see and hear the exorcist. *Failure:* The target has the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions and must move as far from the exorcist as it can on its turns. The effect lasts for 1 minute or until the target takes damage, the exorcist has the Incapacitated condition, or the exorcist dies.

actions.name: Last Rites (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 15, one creature the exorcist can see within 60 feet that isn't a Celestial or Construct (Fiends and Undead have Disadvantage). *Failure:* 36 (**8d8**) Radiant damage. If the target is a Fiend or Undead, it instead takes 64 Radiant damage and is turned to ash if the effect reduces it to 0 Hit Points. *Success* Half damage.

bonusActions.name: Spiritual Healing
bonusActions.value: One creature the exorcist can see regains 35 10d6 Hit Points. Once a creature benefits from Spiritual Healing, it can't do so again until it finishes a Short or Long Rest.

fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is the physical body of an apothecary who has willingly allowed an extraplanar creature to possess them, trapping the powerful outsider in a mortal form. Powerful yet vulnerable, Soulbound Hosts loathe their creators. They wander the world for the means to reverse the curse of mortality placed upon them and return to their otherworldly domains.

Exorcist and Alienist apothecaries do not primarily study the body, and rarely practice the type of magic and science which leads to mutant horrors and flesh-stitched abominations. They are instead concerned with the supernatural forces of the mind and soul. Many research and contact powerful extraplanar entities, eager to possess mortals as a means of entering the material world. These apothecaries learn how to create Soulbound Hosts as a powerful means to contain and fight back against these dangerous otherworldly foes.

fluffInfo.name: Desperate Gambit
fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is usually created under truly desperate circumstances, such as when a heroic apothecary faces a dangerous otherworldly being such as a demon, fey, spirit, or inscrutable entity from the Space Between Worlds. Not only are these planar invaders pernicious foes, many are effectively immortal—often these creatures simply reform when killed outside their native planes. Thus, an apothecary who lacks the ability to defeat the demon on their own, or who wishes to defeat a powerful outsider in a more permanent fashion, may instead decide upon a heroic act of self-sacrifice by turning themselves into a Soulbound Host.

fluffInfo.name: Preparing the Trap
fluffInfo.value: Using an array of implanted metals, ingested tinctures, mental preparations, and occult incantations, a skilled apothecary may willingly prepare their body for possession. During the process, the apothecary can weave a unique spiritual trap. It then falls to the apothecary to convince the otherworldly creature to possess them, an act that many outsiders are eager to do. Thus, the canny apothecary preys on the ego of the monster itself.

fluffInfo.name: Mortal Curse
fluffInfo.value: When the outsider inhabits the body, the apothecary's soul departs, leaving the extraplanar creature to take their place spiritually. If this mortal form is killed or destroyed, the bound creature does not simply return to their plane of origin. Instead, the spirit departs to the afterworlds like any other mortal soul, losing their accumulated otherworldly power forever. Thus, the Soulbound Host becomes both a prison and a death sentence for the other wielding being tricked into the apothecary's body.

fluffInfo.name: Rogue Hosts
fluffInfo.value: Unfortunately, this act of self-sacrifice is not without its imperfections. The apothecary's body is filled with otherworldly essence, and while the creature's power is greatly diminished, they often remain extremely dangerous—allies of the departed apothecary may still find it challenging to slay the Soulbound Host. Many escape, wandering the world with stolen lives and even assuming the identity of their host while they search for the means to escape their now mortal form. All bound outsiders are painfully aware of their new mortality, frustrated that returning to their planes of origin is not a simple matter of destroying their flesh-cage or switching their essence into a different host, one which lacks the binding wards placed by the apothecary.

fluffInfo.name: Price of Freedom

In this way, the apothecary can force the spirit to accept a bargain which requires them to remain in their own worlds for at least the duration of the apothecary's lifetime.

fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is the physical body of an apothecary who has willingly allowed an extraplanar creature to possess them, trapping the powerful outsider in a mortal form. Powerful yet vulnerable, Soulbound Hosts loathe their creators. They wander the world for the means to reverse the curse of mortality placed upon them and return to their otherworldly domains.

Exorcist and Alienist apothecaries do not primarily study the body, and rarely practice the type of magic and science which leads to mutant horrors and flesh-stitched abominations. They are instead concerned with the supernatural forces of the mind and soul. Many research and contact powerful extraplanar entities, eager to possess mortals as a means of entering the material world. These apothecaries learn how to create Soulbound Hosts as a powerful means to contain and fight back against these dangerous otherworldly foes.

fluffInfo.name: Desperate Gambit
fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is usually created under truly desperate circumstances, such as when a heroic apothecary faces a dangerous otherworldly being such as a demon, fey, spirit, or inscrutable entity from the Space Between Worlds. Not only are these planar invaders pernicious foes, many are effectively immortal—often these creatures simply reform when killed outside their native planes. Thus, an apothecary who lacks the ability to defeat the demon on their own, or who wishes to defeat a powerful outsider in a more permanent fashion, may instead decide upon a heroic act of self-sacrifice by turning themselves into a Soulbound Host.

fluffInfo.name: Preparing the Trap
fluffInfo.value: Using an array of implanted metals, ingested tinctures, mental preparations, and occult incantations, a skilled apothecary may willingly prepare their body for possession. During the process, the apothecary can weave a unique spiritual trap. It then falls to the apothecary to convince the otherworldly creature to possess them, an act that many outsiders are eager to do. Thus, the canny apothecary preys on the ego of the monster itself.

fluffInfo.name: Mortal Curse
fluffInfo.value: When the outsider inhabits the body, the apothecary's soul departs, leaving the extraplanar creature to take their place spiritually. If this mortal form is killed or destroyed, the bound creature does not simply return to their plane of origin. Instead, the spirit departs to the afterworlds like any other mortal soul, losing their accumulated otherworldly power forever. Thus, the Soulbound Host becomes both a prison and a death sentence for the other wielding being tricked into the apothecary's body.

fluffInfo.name: Rogue Hosts
fluffInfo.value: Unfortunately, this act of self-sacrifice is not without its imperfections. The apothecary's body is filled with otherworldly essence, and while the creature's power is greatly diminished, they often remain extremely dangerous—allies of the departed apothecary may still find it challenging to slay the Soulbound Host. Many escape, wandering the world with stolen lives and even assuming the identity of their host while they search for the means to escape their now mortal form. All bound outsiders are painfully aware of their new mortality, frustrated that returning to their planes of origin is not a simple matter of destroying their flesh-cage or switching their essence into a different host, one which lacks the binding wards placed by the apothecary.

fluffInfo.name: Price of Freedom
fluffInfo.value: Trapped outsiders can win their freedom by calling back the soul of the apothecary who trapped them, and resurrecting them into their body. This is a thing many outsiders are loathe to do out of fiendish ego, since it puts the original soul in a bargaining position. In this way, the apothecary can force the spirit to accept a bargain which requires them to remain in their own worlds for at least the duration of the apothecary's lifetime.

fluffInfo.value: *When encountering a Fractal Lepidoptera, characters can get stranded in the Border Ethereal Plane. This has the potential to derail a campaign. Here are a few suggestions on how to run this scenario instead:*

entries: When the lepidoptera dies, the fabric of reality temporarily weakens and everyone can safely return to the Prime Material Plane.

Immediately after the lepidoptera dies, the party needs to succeed in a skill challenge to traverse the veil between the planes. Each character can contribute to the skill challenge by suggesting actions that they take to help find the veil, withstand the pull of the Ethereal Plane, and open a gate.
The group succeeds if they make 4 successful DC 15 skill checks before 3 failures.
The characters must harvest the animus of the lepidoptera and craft a fractal key.

fluffInfo.name: Lair effect
fluffInfo.value: Fractal Lepidoptera transform reality around them, manifesting the following effect:

fluffInfo.name: Quantum Entanglement
fluffInfo.value: Creatures taking a Long Rest within 1 mile of the lepidoptera must succeed on a DC 17 Charisma saving throw or gain a pattern effect. Creatures can repeat the saving throw at the end of each Long Rest once they are outside the range of Quantum Entanglement. Casting __Lesser Restoration__ or similar spells of higher level on an affected creature can remove the pattern effect.

table.title: Fractal Lepidoptera Patterns
rows: Something unseen hampers you. You gain the Staggered condition.
On each of your turns, you can only walk in straight lines in the direction of either north, south, east, or west.
Your hands start to flutter uncontrollably. You gain the Clumsy condition.
You can only speak in haikus, rhyming couplets, or iambic pentameter.
You float an inch above the ground. Your walking Speed is unchanged and Difficult Terrain does not affect you.
You gain the ability to see polarized light and the ultraviolet spectrum. You see invisible objects and creatures, and you can see into the Ethereal Plane.

If at least one enemy is Staggered, it targets them with Tessellation. The lepidoptera uses Criss Cross to protect itself from attacks on the border Ethereal Plane.
